clue.text: A figure gone berserk in indignation

indicators.note: something gone berserk is wildly out of control, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: a dud is a failure, a figure who has come to nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper and goes wild with righteous anger.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is loose: a dud is a failure, and the setter seems to treat a figure who has failed that way; the clue may have lost a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in high dudgeon is to feel resentful anger, so the noun is a synonym for indignation.

clue.text: Caught in the act, police being determined

indicators.note: something caught is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a deed is an act
the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's detective police

explanation.surface: The police catch a culprit red-handed and are resolute about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Criminal Investigation Department is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone decided is resolute, firm in purpose, which is a straightforward synonym for determined.

clue.text: Poor diet's corrected, yet he's saving money

indicators.note: a corrected diet has been changed and rearranged, so its letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man fixes his bad eating habits while also putting money aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A depositor puts cash into a bank account, so he is a person keeping savings there.

clue.text: She's caused a large number to leave the US

indicators.note: letters that leave are taken away from the word they belong to

blocks.note: A as written plus M, a thousand in Roman numerals
the country's common name

explanation.surface: A woman is blamed for driving many people out of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a woman's given name, and crosswords often define a name by a pronoun such as she.

clue.text: Game to build modern shopping centre

blocks.note: new means modern
a market is a place to shop

explanation.surface: A developer plans to put up an up-to-date mall.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is a card game, also the name of an English racing town.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a gambling card game in which players stake chips on cards laid out on the table.

clue.text: Building worker going around double-parking - and he drinks!

indicators.note: a word going around another surrounds it, so one piece is wrapped about the other

blocks.note: a tradesman who lays tiles
P for parking, doubled

explanation.surface: A builder who parks badly also turns out to be fond of a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the standard road-sign abbreviation for parking.
explanation.definitionFit: A tippler habitually drinks alcohol, so the noun describes a man who drinks often.

clue.text: Little bird with the French name

blocks.note: the tit is a small songbird
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A small bird is given a French name.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name of a book, film or song, or a form of address, so the two nouns match.

clue.text: "The Player" by one-time joiner

indicators.note: a joiner fixes pieces together, here hinting that the two parts are simply butted end to end

blocks.note: per means by, as in per post
former means one-time or previous

explanation.surface: A film title is credited to a man who used to work as a carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: A joiner is a woodworking tradesman; here the word only asks for the two parts to be fitted together.
explanation.definitionFit: A player in a drama or band is someone who performs, so a performer is a player.

clue.text: Don't take a vacation

blocks.note: first meaning: to ... something behind rather than carry it off
second meaning: time off work, a holiday

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like advice to skip a holiday; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to let something remain where it is, while the noun is permitted time away from work.

clue.text: Waves may be put in the hair

definitions.text: may be put in the hair

blocks.note: first meaning: long swelling waves of the sea

blocks.clueFragment: may be put in the hair
blocks.note: second meaning: cylinders used to curl hair

explanation.surface: Hairdressing advice on setting waves with curlers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a hair-styling tip, but the waves are those of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Big ocean breakers are called this, and so are the curlers wound into hair to set it.

clue.text: An island in mid-Atlantic, a primates' paradise

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of Atlantic, the word a and the start of primates

explanation.surface: An Atlantic island that is a haven for apes and monkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: The island is in fact in the Bay of Naples, not the Atlantic; 'paradise' is a description of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is a famous Italian island resort off the Sorrento peninsula, long regarded as a beauty spot.

clue.text: The ebbing tide?

blocks.note: surface reading: the sea going out as the tide turns
setter's reading: water that is dropping, a cascade over a cliff

explanation.walkthrough: An ebbing tide is water falling in level; the answer takes the phrase literally as water falling over a drop.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade where a river drops over a ledge is literally water falling, which the falling tide suggests.

clue.text: In time ill-assorted pairs will get contrary

indicators.note: things ill-assorted are badly sorted, so the letters come in a jumbled order
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: a date is a point in time
pairs with its letters mixed

explanation.surface: Couples badly matched will in time start disagreeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparate things are essentially different and opposed, so they are contrary to one another.

clue.text: Over-large order given by heartless woman

indicators.note: without a heart, a word loses its middle letter

blocks.note: the Order of the British Empire
she is a woman

explanation.surface: A tyrannical woman hands out an excessive command.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour, an order of chivalry; a heartless SHE drops its middle H.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obese is very overweight, carrying far too much body fat, so larger than healthy.

clue.text: An individual very keen on taking note in staff turnover

indicators.note: a turnover turns something over, so the word reads back to front
taking means holding something inside

blocks.note: a rod is a staff or stick
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic employee keeps track of staff coming and going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff turnover' looks like an employment phrase, but staff is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A doter dotes on someone, being foolishly or excessively fond, so a person keen on another.

clue.text: Control the way everything is put back

blocks.note: to rein is to control
St is street, a way
all means everything

explanation.surface: An instruction for rebuilding controls: everything goes back where it was.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstall is to install again, putting equipment or software back in its place.

clue.text: Royalty with a touching way of getting rich

definitions.text: Royalty with a touching way of getting rich

blocks.clueFragment: Royalty with a touching way of getting rich
blocks.note: surface reading: a monarch who becomes wealthy in some moving or sentimental manner
setter's reading: a ruler whose touch literally turned things to gold

explanation.walkthrough: Touching seems to mean moving; it means making contact.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this Phrygian ruler was granted the power to turn everything he touched into gold.

clue.text: Never sins - could be due to angst

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else once rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A person who never does wrong may be driven by anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is anxious dread, and nerviness is a state of jumpy anxiety, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: A shady hemisphere?

blocks.note: surface reading: a half of the globe in shadow
setter's reading: a half-world, in French terms, of disreputable people

explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase literally means half-world, matching hemisphere, and shady means of dubious reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a class of women or society on the fringes of respectability, kept by wealthy lovers.

clue.text: A lawyer railing about a highly-regarded person

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: a railing is a barrier
St is a saint, a person held in high regard

explanation.surface: An attorney complains bitterly about some esteemed figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Railing looks like the verb for ranting; it is the noun for a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister is a lawyer entitled to argue cases in the higher courts in Britain.

clue.text: Loaf, which is a mistake

blocks.note: first meaning: a long crusty loaf of white bread
second meaning: an embarrassing blunder

explanation.surface: Idling about is called an error.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaf looks like a verb, to idle; it is a type of bread loaf in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the word names a crusty bread loaf and, informally, a howler or blunder.

clue.text: Continue to strike a man

blocks.note: to ram is to strike
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: An order to keep hitting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Continue to strike reads as ram on, to keep ramming.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramon is a Spanish given name for a male, so it can be clued simply as a man.

clue.text: Mark admits "X" returned for the music

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
admits means lets inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to note is to mark
X is ten in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A teacher concedes a cross was sent back for the score.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonette is a composition for nine performers, so it is a piece of music.

clue.text: Goes off without the right when ugly customers appear

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
without here means outside, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: goes with its letters mixed
R abbreviates right

explanation.surface: A party leaves without turning right when unpleasant people turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: Without looks like lacking but is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly customer is a nasty, intimidating person, and ogres are brutish monsters of that kind.

clue.text: The revolutionary head limits breaks

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of revolutionary
limits are ends

explanation.surface: The leader of a revolt sets restrictions.
explanation.definitionFit: To rend is to tear apart, so rends is a synonym for breaks in the verb sense.

clue.text: Jack's molars - in a bad state

indicators.note: in a bad state the letters are disordered and must be rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Jack has very poor teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack, or Jack Tar, is old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack is traditional slang for a seaman, and a sailorman is a sailor.

clue.text: Relish disrespectful talk

blocks.note: first meaning: a condiment
second meaning: cheek, impudence

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys being rude.
explanation.walkthrough: Relish looks like a verb, to enjoy; it is a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a condiment served with food and, informally, cheeky impertinent backchat.

clue.text: One gets mad about short measure time after time

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
about means around, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: one with its letters mixed
ft is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: Someone gets angry repeatedly at being given short measures.
explanation.walkthrough: Short measure reads like being cheated of drink, but means an abbreviated unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, happening repeatedly, which is what time after time expresses.

clue.text: Great painting? Far from it!

blocks.note: surface reading: a masterpiece of art
setter's reading: great means big, so the opposite is a tiny picture

explanation.walkthrough: Great suggests excellence; the setter means size.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature is a very small, finely detailed painting, often a portrait, the opposite of a large canvas.

clue.text: Opinion that is not irreversible

indicators.note: something not irreversible can be turned round and still stand, so it reads the same both ways

blocks.note: a word that survives being turned round, reading the same in both directions

explanation.surface: A view that can still be changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true, so it is an opinion or doctrine.

clue.text: To tackle the problem yet again called for fortitude

blocks.note: the prefix re- means again
to solve is to tackle a problem

explanation.surface: Having another go at the problem took grit.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve is firm determination, and fortitude is courage in adversity, close synonyms for steadfastness.

clue.text: Faithful as serving men

blocks.note: as and since both mean because
the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

explanation.surface: Loyal, as soldiers are expected to be.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sincere is genuine and honest, and faithful can mean true and honest in the same way.
